newsitem.title: USA: Food Lion benefits from ABC show-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Food Lion benefits from ABC show-analysts.

text.p: While supermarket chain Food Lion Inc suffered sunken profits after a hidden-camera report by the ABC television network in 1992, the expose also prompted changes in operations that today have the grocer poised to earn some of its highest results in years, analysts said on Thursday.
Food Lion, which sought to boost sales in the 1980s and early 1990s by adding stores, switched its focus to improving productivity at existing stores, the analysts said.
"They trained employees better, did a better job at keeping stores clean and watching more closely the out-of-date markers," said Kenneth Gassman at Davenport & Co.
As a result, Food Lion was expected to earn $0.44 per share in 1996 versus $0.36 a share the previous year.
Analysts said that the ABC news report on televvision was a defininig moment for the company.
"What happened afterward was sales fell off a cliff and that gave top management a wake-up call and they have been working hard to make the stores a better place to shop," Wilder said.
In 1992, Food Lion earned $0.37 a share but the results tumbled to $0.01 a share in 1993.

"The company felt the pressure of the broadcast in all of 1993," Gassman said. "Then, in 1994 we began to see some signs of a recovery which continued into 1995, but it wasn't until the beginning of 1996 that Food Lion's sales began to show sharp gains reminiscent of the late 1980s and early 1990s."

The analysts agreed the rebound more accurately reflects improved productivity since only 100 stores have been added to the Food Lion chain since the PrimeTime Live broadcast, bringing the total to 1112 today.
By the end of 1996, some 40 percent of the stores were either new or had been remodeled since the end of 1993.
Wilder said Food Lion was also pressured by competitors whose grocery stores include bakeries and delicatessens
"They were aware that they needed to do some things from a merchandising standpoint but were moving slowly," Wilder said.
Sanitation, improper food-handling practices, and the sale of out-dated merchandise were issues in ABC's report.
ABC is a unit of the Walt Disney Co.

Food Lion sued and argued in federal court in Greensboro, North Carolina that had ABC's undercover producers done their jobs as Food Lion workers none of the spoiled meats or other bad foods would have been sold.
On Wednesday a federal jury awarded Food Lion, a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION' SA, $5.5 million in punitive damages from ABC for fraud, trespass and breach of loyalty.
But the victory has not benefitted the stock, according to analysts. Shares of Food Lion closed off 1/4 at 8-7/8 on Thursday.

"Winning the suit is a psychic plus," as it conveys some sense that ABC was wrong, said Interstate/Johnson Lane analyst Lee Wilder. But whether there was a grain of truth in the Nov. 5, 1992 report is irrelevant, she added.
